title: Why young dancers lack proteges
summary: Asked why masters no longer have protégés, Green says dancers do not fraternise, the woman interviewer suggests schools, and Green names Jimmy Slyde and Sandman Sims as teachers.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well, the one thing I noticed though is that tap dancing isn't really being passed on like it used to be in the old days. Some of the old masters used to have protégés, and the dancers of today don't have proteges like they used to. How do you account for that?

Well, that's because they don't buddy-buddy. They don't fraternize enough with -- well, there's one that does it. I think he's -- what did -- George Nuremberg, that's Nipsy Russell's protégé. Sandman. I think he has done this, Sandman Sims, see. Because -- do you understand? He is a Hooper, you know. You see, they're on-the-town dancer, you see. He has an idol also.
Well, maybe it's just that a tap -- tap dancing today for the young people doesn't have relevance like it did in the older days.
Yes. It has it but you must -- like I

say -- fraternize with these people, see. Now, I have -- I have been having to look out myself, you know. I've been trying to look out to try to like rediscover a Rough Rider, see, which is -- he's a gentleman I've seen. I don't know whether he -- he knows most of the ballrooms, you know. He knows most of those type of dances, but he's a great father, see. He's got about -- he's a parent of about seven or eight children, you know. And --
Have you had any luck in finding people -- young people to carry on your craft?

Yeah. Well, I think he could be one of them, you know, because he has the -- I call him Dancing Man, you know. He's something like the early brother, (unintelligible) Berry of the Berry Brothers, you see, (unintelligible) see.

So, I think if you're not open to teaching, say, open school where you -- where one can spot talent, a talented pupil. This is how you find protégés. You can't just bump into one in the street, or while you're shopping or something. You have to be at a school where there's so many different people with sort of an urge to want to dance, or be in this kind of work. And then you can spot the ones that have an extra edge over the others. They're the ones that have it. They're the ones that can get into the more difficult parts of this work. They become a protege.
Well, is tap dancing being taught

Well, individually I can say there's two parents in the Hoofers that does it properly, you see. One of them is teaching professors in Europe. That's the Good Father. That's Jimmy Slde, you see. And the other one is Nipsy Russell's protege, see. Somewhere's in District of Columbus, you see.

Yeah. Well, the Godfather of the quotations, you see. But I'm in the throes of discovery, see, because I have a great hope for someone that I think is going to be another early master, see, like the scratch rock was to the Injuns. I guess you'd -- (Recording interruption)
